entries.title: Fourier entropy increment under Boolean coordinate restriction
entries.statement: On the uniformly measured d-dimensional Boolean cube, let f:{-1,1}^d->{-1,1}. Write hat(f)(S)=E[f(x)product_{j in S}x_j], H(f)=sum_S hat(f)(S)^2 log_2(1/hat(f)(S)^2), I_i(f)=sum_{S containing i}hat(f)(S)^2, and Delta_i(f)=H(f)-(H(f|x_i=+1)+H(f|x_i=-1))/2, with zero entropy terms interpreted as zero. A constant function has H=I=0.

entries.title: Refuted route: every coordinate has bounded entropy/influence increment
entries.statement: REFUTED ROUTE, supported by an author proof awaiting independent check: the proposed quantifiers are 'there exists finite K such that for every d>=1, every Boolean f on the uniform d-cube, and every coordinate i, Delta_i(f)<=K I_i(f)', where Delta is the base-2 Fourier entropy increment under restriction. The stronger 'every coordinate' quantifier must not be substituted for the existential coordinate in a restriction induction.
assumptions: Every coordinate, not an existential choice

entries.title: Draft Boolean witness: bad coordinate cost diverges while FEI holds
entries.statement: DRAFT RESULT; author derivation, independent check pending. For every even n=2m>=4, define g(x)=product_{j=1}^m(1+x_{2j-1}+x_{2j}-x_{2j-1}x_{2j})/2 and F(x,t)=g(x)-(1-t)1{x=(1,...,1)} for x in {-1,1}^n, t in {-1,1}. These functions are Boolean. Under uniform measure and base-2 Fourier entropy, p=I_t(F)=2^{-n} and Delta_t(F)=H(F)-(H(F|t=1)+H(F|t=-1))/2>=np. Nonetheless I(F)=n/2+(n+1)p and H(F)<=2I(F). This is an obstruction to an arbitrary-coordinate linear increment bound, not to FEI or to an existential good-coordinate bound.

entries.title: Draft exact logarithmic coordinate cost
entries.statement: DRAFT RESULT; author derivation, independent check pending. For every uniform-cube Boolean f and coordinate i with p=I_i(f), its base-2 Fourier entropy increment Delta_i=H(f)-(H(f|i=1)+H(f|i=-1))/2 satisfies 0<=Delta_i<=h_2(p)+(2/ln2)p<=p log_2(1/p)+(3/ln2)p, using zero conventions at p=0. Here h_2 is binary entropy. The additive constant is exact: sup_{d,f,i:p>0}(Delta_i/p-log_2(1/p))=3/ln2. The upper bound follows from a paired-spectrum decomposition and a Jensen-Shannon/Hellinger comparison; the disjoint-pair Boolean selector witnesses attain the supremum in the limit. This bound does not solve general FEI.

entries.title: Draft conditional FEI reduction to small coordinate influences
entries.statement: DRAFT CONDITIONAL REDUCTION; author rederivation, independent check pending. Fix 0<tau<1 independently of dimension. If all uniformly measured Boolean functions whose coordinate influences are all <tau satisfy H(f)<=C_tau I(f) with C_tau independent of dimension and base-2 Fourier entropy, then every Boolean function satisfies H(f)<=max(C_tau,log_2(1/tau)+3/ln2) I(f). Repeatedly restrict a coordinate of influence >=tau; the dimension decreases and the exact influence identity telescopes with the coordinate entropy bound. The converse is immediate. The required low-influence class estimate remains unproved here; selecting a maximum-influence coordinate is not asserted to solve that remaining case.
assumptions: Assumed low-influence bound covers every dimension

relations.rationale: For each fixed K, the quoted Boolean witness has an even n>K and Delta_t/I_t>=n, contradicting the proposed every-coordinate bound. This edge does not target general FEI.
The witness concerns the defined Delta_t under the stated entropy and influence normalization.
The bound and supremum use this exact normalized coordinate entropy increment.
Optimality of the additive constant uses the explicit witness and its analytic limit; the upper bound has a separate JS proof.
For p>=tau the quoted logarithmic coordinate bound is at most p(log_2(1/tau)+3/ln2), supplying the branching-node estimate in the finite restriction tree.
